prompt: Write the body (about 150 words) of an insurer's answer to a personal injury petition in Texas: a general denial and three affirmative defenses that fit a low-speed head-on collision. Plain text. Call the parties only 'Plaintiff' and 'Defendant'. No names, placeholders, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1490; do not mention it.)
text:
Defendant generally denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition and demands strict proof thereof as required by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure. Pursuant to Rule 92, Defendant also asserts the following affirmative defenses.

First, Plaintiff's alleged injuries were not proximately caused by the incident in question. The impact between the vehicles was of low speed and minor force, and any condition Plaintiff now claims was pre-existing, degenerative, or unrelated to the collision.

Second, Plaintiff failed to exercise ordinary care to mitigate damages, including by failing to follow reasonable medical advice and by incurring treatment that was unnecessary or unreasonable in cost. Any recovery must be reduced accordingly.

Third, to the extent Plaintiff's own negligence contributed to the occurrence, Defendant invokes the proportionate responsibility provisions of Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code. Any recovery must be reduced by Plaintiff's percentage of responsibility, and bars recovery if that percentage exceeds fifty percent.
